newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks trend stronger in morning.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks trend stronger in morning.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks headed into positive territory Thursday morning after a weak start, boosted by a rebound in oversold property shares and the positive sentiment surrounding red and pink chips, brokers said.
"We opened low because the Dow had a bad day yesterday," said Franco Tong in institutional sales at New China Hong Kong. "But the red chips are still going strong pre-handover."
The Hang Seng Index was trading 95 points higher at 14,299, after dipping to 14,137 in early trade. Turnover was a robust HK$4.6 billion in the first 40 minutes of the session.
The Dow Industrials shed 42.07 points, or 0.54 percent, to 7,718.71 overnight, chiefly on worries over earnings shortfalls in the technology sector.
The property sector led Hong Kong blue chips higher. The newly launched Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporations Index continued its rally, advancing 3.43 percent to 3,086.

"Property stocks are gradually discounting the package laid out by C.Y. Leung," said Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas. C.Y. Leung, future Hong Kong leader Tung Chee-hwa's advisor on property, has completed a report on the property market but its contents have not yet been revealed.
Property development and construction activity remains one of key economic sectors of Hong Kong.
"If the measures are not too harsh, then we should see property stocks stabilise," said Mak
Henderson Land was the best performing property share, up HK$1.25 to HK$66.00, rebounding from recent weakness, brokers said.
Banking giant HSBC Holdings added HK$1.00 to HK$225.00 and subisidiary Hang Seng Bank advanced HK$0.25 to HK$92.50.
Hutchison Whampoa lost HK$0.50 to HK$59.75.
The red chip index was boosted chiefly by a jump in China Resources Enterprises. The share advanced to a new all-time high of HK$32.10, then eased to trade HK$2.90 higher at HK$30.60.
The company announced it would spend HK$2.77 billion to a stake in Hongkong Chinese Bank, subsidiary of The HKCB Bank Holding Co Ltd, and concrete manufacturing operations from its parent company.
Hopewell gained HK$0.175 to HK$4.275, on the rumours the company is in talks with China Everbright-IHD on that company's taking a stake in Hopewell.
China Everbright-IHD was the second most actively traded issue after China Resources, rising HK$0.30 to HK$17.55.
